newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM asks for probe into PZU premiums rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM asks for probe into PZU premiums rise.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Friday asked the Anti-Monopoly Office to check if the rise of motor liability insurance premiums by the country's largest PZU insurer was monopolistic practice.

On Thursday the state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), which has an 80 percent share in Poland's obligatory motor insurance market with 9.5 million customers, announced it would raise the premiums by 43 percent as of December 27.

"...I kindly request that your Office starts an investigation if PZU's action has monopolistic character," a statement by the government press office quoted Cimoszewicz's letter to the head of the Anti-Monopoly Office.
PZU has said the move was forced by a more than 41 percent rise in obligatory motor insurance damages in the last two years by booming new car registrations and worsening road safety.
